references.text: The Levites were given cities to live in among all the tribes of Israel, which explains why a Levite could come from any of the gates of Israel.
The Levites were given cities scattered throughout Israel, confirming their settlement pattern mentioned in Deuteronomy.
The Levites had no inheritance share in the land but depended on service at the sanctuary, which motivated their desire to go to the place the Lord chose.
The place the Lord chooses for His name to dwell is central to worship, and the Levites were entitled to serve there.
The chosen place where the Levites and priests served was the center of justice and spiritual guidance in Israel.
A Levite living in Bethlehem in Judah illustrates how Levites lived scattered throughout Israel and could travel to other places to serve.
Under King Hezekiah, the Levites were called to come and serve at the temple, in line with their right to serve at the chosen place.
